title: Colored Weingarten Calculus for Block-Unitary Ensemble
abstract: Haar randomness is the standard null model for quantum typicality, scrambling, and random-matrix formulations of thermalization. In many physical settings, however, randomness is naturally constrained to subspaces of Hilbert space. This structure arises, in particular, both in systems with symmetry-resolved sectors and in the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH), where mesoscopic energy windows define subspaces in which nearby energy eigenstates are mixed. Motivated by these settings, we consider a Block-Unitary Ensemble consisting of independently Haar-random unitaries acting on each subspace. We develop a constructive Weingarten Calculus for this ensemble, providing a unified framework across quantum information and many-body physics. This construction reveals a symmetry-resolved Schur-Weyl duality, where the relevant commutant is not the ordinary permutation algebra, but the one of color-preserving permutations. We apply this framework to quantum states under symmetry constraints and to energy-resolved ensembles for ETH.
summary: This paper introduces a 'Colored Weingarten Calculus' to analyze quantum systems constrained by symmetries, modeled by the Block-Unitary Ensemble. It develops a mathematical framework showing that the system's dynamics are governed by color-preserving permutations rather than standard permutations. This has direct applications to understanding thermalization in many-body systems and quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper develops a constructive Weingarten Calculus for the Block-Unitary Ensemble to provide a unified mathematical framework for systems where quantum randomness is constrained by symmetries.
main_result: The calculus reveals a symmetry-resolved Schur-Weyl duality, showing that the average of operators is governed by color-preserving permutations, leading to a block-diagonal structure in the Gram matrix.
method: The authors calculate Haar moments and Gram matrix elements by analyzing the commutant of the collective unitary action, generalizing permutation group theory to color-preserving permutations.
model_or_system: The model is the Block-Unitary Ensemble, $U(H|M) = U(H_1) 	imes \cdots 	imes U(H_m)$, which describes quantum systems whose Hilbert space is decomposed into independent symmetry-resolved subspaces. This is motivated by contexts like the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH).
key_observables: The $k$-th order twirling map $\Phi^{(k)} U(H|M)(O^{\otimes k})$ and the resulting correlation functions $\langle O^U_{ij} angle$ are key observables.
important_parameters: The number of subspaces ($m$), the replica number ($k$), the dimension of each subspace ($d_i$), and the occupation vector $\mathbf{n}$ are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system dynamics can be effectively modeled by independent Haar-random unitaries acting on symmetry-constrained subspaces, allowing for the use of the Block-Unitary Ensemble.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the block-unitary matrix structure (Fig. 1) and the block-diagonal factorization of the Weingarten matrix based on the occupation vector (Fig. 2).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the Block-Unitary Ensemble and its commutant (Chunk 2), then deriving the general form of the Gram matrix elements using color-preserving permutations (Chunk 3), and finally applying this calculus to calculate correlation functions in the energy eigenbasis (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, general mathematical tools (Weingarten Calculus) to analyze thermalization and quantum scrambling in many-body systems that possess underlying symmetries, bridging quantum information theory and condensed matter physics.
